claim: Acceptance criteria omit the brief-locked Picard demo identity. AC (ii) only requires that some username/email/full_name/address render after demo login, so a profile page that still shows "Demo User" / demo@quantumbank.com could satisfy §8 while missing the product requirement in brief §2.5. recommended_change: Extend AC (ii) (and optionally add AC (vi)) so that after demo login on a freshly initialized DB, the body includes Jean-Luc Picard, jpicard@starfleet.fed, and the brief address (or the chosen apostrophe-safe substring). Keep the stale-local-DB caveat in R3.

SUMMARY: The plan is approvable as-is. Grounding is strong on the load-bearing pilot facts (no migration/ALTER path, count-gated seed, subset-only drift guard, SELECT * at get_user_by_username), fork (b) is the correct least-scope call with an honest deferral list, boundaries (auth redirect, no object id, fail-closed missing subject, allow-listed projection) match the brief and improve on the dashboard’s session full_name pattern, and the test plan is mostly falsifiable (including no-leak-on-redirect, key-set equality, created_at absence, stale session). Scope stays one read-only service; out-of-scope is honest. No blocker/high issues. Before or during reconciliation, disposition the mediums: bind Picard in §8 acceptance criteria, complete the PRD §5.2 risk columns (especially review triggers), and add one DB-vs-session source-of-truth case so §4 is enforced by tests rather than intent alone.
